newsitem.title: UK: UK Tourist Authority drops Union Jack, sparks fury.
newsitem.headline: UK Tourist Authority drops Union Jack, sparks fury.

text.p: The British Tourist Authority on Wednesday sparked a bout of nationalist fury by deciding to drop the distinctive Union Jack flag as its logo.

Politicians, academics and editorialists united to condemn the move. "What jackasses at the British Tourist Authority. How dare they drop our proud Union flag as our emblem," thundered the Sun tabloid.

The authority, which promotes the 40 billion pound industry worldwide, said it was opting for a new logo because the Union Jack had a "triumphal, colonial feel to it that won't go down well in certain parts of the world."
"What cringe-making claptrap," said The Daily Mail in an editorial on the red, white and blue flag. "Why this headlong retreat from national pride?" it asked.
The decision follows a similar move by the airline British Airways which dropped the flag from its tail fins and replaced it with assorted ethnic logos.
Legislators from both sides of the political divide united to berate the authority, which represents one of the country's five largest industries that employs 1.7 million people.
"If the new logo is as stupid looking as the British Airways one, this will turn out to be a waste of time and money," said Labour member of parliament Kate Hoey.
Opposition Conservative Lady Olga Maitland agreed: "This is outrageous. How can they do it? It appears that we are ashamed to be British and I am sure there will be an outcry."
Britain once boasted an empire of 400 million subjects that spanned the globe. But in today's post-colonial era, Britons feel some uncertainty about waving the flag on the world stage.

Historian Dr David Starkey of the London School of Economics bemoaned this loss of identity, telling the Daily Mail: "There has been a complete collapse of a sense of national identity. There is a vacuum."

The Irish Tourist Board was forced to back down when it moved to drop the shamrock as its instantly recognisable emblem. Opponents of the British Tourist Authority plan hope that history will repeat itself.
The greatest outrage was expressed by a bowler-hatted British gentleman in a pinstripe suit.

His moustache bristled with outrage when he told BBC Television: "We fought for the Union Jack. People died for the Union Jack. It marked every country in the British Empire. If the Tourist Board wants to ban it, they should disband the bloody Tourist Board."
